We receive total bytes billed for all our queries in world_fishing_827. We compare the amount of TB billed per day against a constant value to ensure we are not accidentally causing unexpected costs.

We receive total bytes billed for all our queries in world_fishing_827. We compare the amount of TB billed per day against the maximum amount over a sliding window to ensure we are not accidentally causing unexpected costs. This is broken down by service account users (dimension=true) vs non-service account users (dimension=false).

A GFW API scraper downloads data from our API in regular intervals. By looking at the latest available timestamps in each API endpoint we can check whether any data is delayed. The delay is calculated as the time since the expected publication and only exists when data was not available at the expected publication time.
Fishing events can show anomalies that we don't see by just observing fishing effort, particularly across the day boundary. The hourly granularity allows us to see these anomalies.

Fishing events can show anomalies that we don't see by just observing fishing effort. This configuration is filtered for flag='ESP' which has some of the cleanest periodical patterns of all countries. The hourly granularity allows us to see deviations from the periodical pattern which are only expected due to human behaviour that the mstl model does not account for, like dynamic holidays (e.g. Easter).

The monitoring pipeline gathers statistics for S2 published detections. By looking at the latest available timestamps we can check whether publication data is delayed. The delay is calculated as the time since the expected publication and only exists when data was not available at the expected publication time. The expected publication time is the minimum delay based on all historical publications.

The monitoring pipeline gathers statistics for the S2 index. By looking at the latest available timestamps we can check whether the index is delayed. The delay is calculated as the time since the expected publication and only exists when data was not available at the expected publication time. The expected publication time is the minimum delay based on all historical publications.
